text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: gateway service returning elevated 502/504 rate (p95 latency up). Current 5xx rate 8% over 5m. Pager: PD-4931.

sara: I see a spike starting ~1765432050, correlates with a deploy?

matt: Not seeing a commit in prod around that time. kube events look normal.

jon: Logs for the gateway show a lot of upstream timeouts but most requests are missing request-id and route tags. our trace sampling is also 0.5% so we have almost no traces for the affected window. Big observability gap.

anya: Confirmed — log lines for /v1/generate are sparse. I think a recent change in the ingress filter dropped a header we rely on for request-id propagation.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-043. Severity: P1 (customer impact).

sara: Quick customer impact summary for CSE: error spikes for text-generation endpoints, affecting small fraction of requests but high-priority customers seeing increased latency/502. Will update.

matt: Trying to reproduce locally with same traffic pattern, hitting timeouts on backend pool: many connections show stalled KV-cache lookups. Could be overloaded model nodes or a circuit breaker misfire.

jon: Ops, can you check envoy config on gateway-1/2? suspecting header_mangling filter change from yesterday. If request-id is missing, tracing -> sampling doesn't attach spans so debugging is blind.

anya: I'm going to add a stopgap log that logs upstream status + raw headers for 1% of requests to capture samples. Will patch gateway-configmap and roll one replica.

matt: Good. Also can we temporarily increase trace sampling to 5% for the gateway? Need more traces to correlate upstream timeouts.

jon: I'll open a hotpatch:

```
kubectl -n prod patch deployment gateway -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"debug-logs":"true"}}}}}'
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/gateway TRACE_SAMPLING=0.05
```

incident-bot: @sara @matt @jon Annotations: please include runbook steps and rollback plan in the incident doc.

ops-next-oncall: Oncall here — I'll scale up the model pool by +20% and enable connection timeout backoff adjustments. Scaling now.

sara: Noted. Can someone validate request-id propagation after the config patch? If it's still missing, we need to add a middleware that injects X-Request-Id for any incoming request as a stopgap.

anya: Patch applied to gateway-configmap. Rolling gateway-1. Logs for the next 120s should show extra debug entries for sampling.

matt: I see new debug entries. Sampling traces are coming in. Traces show a pattern: 502s occur when backend returns 504 then gateway converts to 502 due to header mapping default. The backend pool nodes are returning 504 intermittently — likely overloaded.

jon: Can you paste a sample trace id?

matt: trace: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00 (sanitized). Backend host: model-node-12; upstream latency 18s before timeout.

sara: Customer impact update: high-volume customers on us-east-1 saw increased errors between 09:05–09:18 PDT. Recommending a status page update and an outbound email to top 10 affected accounts.

ops-next-oncall: Scaling finished. Also bumped backend keepalive and timeout thresholds to reduce spurious circuit trips.

anya: I'm still seeing some requests without X-Request-Id. Applying a quick ingress middleware to inject when missing:

```
# nginx lua snippet
local id = ngx.req.get_headers()["X-Request-Id"]
if not id then
  ngx.req.set_header("X-Request-Id", ngx.time() .. "-" .. ngx.worker.pid())
end
```

incident-bot: Note: please coordinate with security if you add headers that could affect logging compliance.

matt: With injected ids and increased sampling, traces show the root cause: a subset of model nodes (12,13) are stuck at high GC and refuse new inference sessions. GC correlated with a recent quantization switch for that shard. Rolling back quantization experiment on nodes 12/13 now.

ops-next-oncall: Rolling rollback: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo statefulset/model-pool --to-revision=42`

anya: Rollback complete on model-node-12/13. I'm watching error rate.

matt: 5xx rate dropping — from 8% down to 1.2% over 10m. Latency p95 also improving.

sara: Great. I'll draft a customer-facing postmortem and a short internal blameless timeline. Key action items: (1) fix header propagation tests in CI, (2) increase baseline trace sampling for ingress, (3) add liveliness checks for quantization experiments, (4) add temporary middleware to inject request-id if missing.

jon: Also recommend adding a fallback route policy in smart-routing so gateway can reroute to healthy model pool if node-level health fails.

incident-bot: Handoff: @matt you take primary for follow-up remediation and postmortem. @anya you're primary for observability fixes and patch PR. Next oncall: @ops-next-oncall take after 30m.

matt: Ack. I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups. Creating INC-2026-043-ops ticket with links and runbooks.

sara: I'll draft the succinct customer impact note and coordinate with CSE for outbound.

anya: I'll open PRs for the ingress middleware + increased trace sampling + CI tests.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Please update incident doc with timeline and link to PRs before closing. :white_check_mark:
